data.body:
Fixes bug B-merged-uncompleted-claimable: In the gap between ddflow merge (lease released) and ddflow complete, ddflow next offers the merged item as ready and a claim by ANY other agent succeeds as a rework: item.reworked clears every gate, so the merging lane's complete is refused (implement, unit_tests, merge 'not run') and the second lane holds an empty item. Hit by 3 stub lanes in a sandbox in the first full run of SW-pilot-toy (toy-08: lane-1 merge 13:57:23, lane-2 claim 13:57:24 and item.reworked with the merged sha), and reproduced by hand with two agents: merge as lane-1, next as lane-2 lists it, claim as lane-2 exits 0, complete as lane-1 exits 3. Every parallel fleet has this race; any pull lane (SW-pull) makes it routine. The re-claim route of fix-B-rework-of-merged-item-keeps-stale-merge is for a deliberate rework. Direction: next does not offer an item with a merge and no completion, and a claim of one by an agent other than the merger is refused unless it says it means rework. Regression test: two agents, merge then next and claim, gates intact and complete passes. SW-pilot-toy works around it by never letting a lane claim an item another lane took in the run; real lanes share no such board. Found on SW-pilot-toy.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-merged-uncompleted-claimable --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-merged-uncompleted-claimable --regression-test <test>` first).

Findings from lane fix-mergedclaim (2026-11-05). Never claimed, no code written, nothing run against the unfixed code: all of this comes from reading main, so treat the design as a proposal. Stopped by D-unwind-for-kilo-2026-11-05.

Blockers seen: DX-reserved-slot (sw-reservedslot) held _readiness.py, _plan.py and core/schedule/__init__.py, lease live at 19:19Z, with unit_tests recorded partial 19:19:10Z. Lane high1 also has a lease.waiting on this item, renewed about every 11 min until at least 18:48Z, but no `ddflow wait` process of its was found at 18:56Z; check whether it is still alive before claiming.

Proposed design:
1. Refuse inside `_acquire_locked` (ddflow/services/leases/claim.py), next to the plan_blocker check, not in a claim guard. The guard reads the fold from the top of `_claim_once`, so a claim that folded before the merge would pass it; the DONE check there exists for the same stale-snapshot reason. Keep the word --force out of the refusal, or claim() routes an agent to `_claim_by_approval`.
2. `next`: add a non-lease filter with `register_filter` in core/schedule/_filters.py (runs last, so existing blocks such as an expired lease keep their wording). item_blocker also feeds `wait` through reservations.py, while L.acquire only calls plan_blocker, so the filter does not stop the merger's or a rework claim. tests/test_plan_pipeline.py:106-107 pins the FILTERS list and must change with it. A filter in _filters.py would not need _plan.py.
3. Trap: `_h_reopened` clears gates but KEEPS merged_sha, so a bare `merged_sha and not terminal` test hides every `verify --reopen` item from the queue. Proposed predicate: merged_sha and not terminal and (not it.reopened or gate_outcome('merge') == 'passed').
4. Merger identity: the merge gate's `by`, or the agent of the last worktree.merged event. merge writes worktree.merged, then lease.released, then gate.passed merge, seconds apart under load, so the gate can be missing in the gap; a non-merger is refused either way.
5. Saying it means rework: a new `--rework` claim flag (Param in surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py incl. tool_order, lifecycle_cli.py claim call, api/lifecycle/claim.py claim and _claim_once, acquire). `--force` is not enough: agents cannot use it (B49fa10bbb1), so their rework would need an operator approval. This is a choice the item does not settle, and it needs globs beyond the four declared: services/leases/claim.py, _filters.py, the two surface files, tests/test_plan_pipeline.py, plus the shared goldens.
6. Not verified: whether a lane other than the merger can `complete` a merged item. The blocked reason should name the true route, since a crashed merger's item no longer appears in `next`.

Regression tests to write (tests/test_rework_merged_item_reopens_merge.py, agents via `--agent`, pass_pipeline omit merge): next hides the item from both lanes and names `ddflow complete`; lane-2 claim exits 3, gates and merged_sha intact, lane-1 complete exits 0; L.acquire raises directly for lane-2; lane-2 `--rework` reopens; the merger re-claims with no flag; a reopened item is offered and claimable.
